messages.subject: Model comparison in different habitats
parts:
Hi,
I am currently trying to analyze my data from a bird point survey I
conducted in urban and semi-urban environments and have been contemplating
on the way I can compare the different models that have been fitted by
program DISATNCE. To be more specific, if I want to get a density estimate
for each location each model fitted has different chi, AIC, log-likelihood
and variance values, on what basis can I compare the models and
the =93power=94 of the model.
In addition I would appreciate it if I could get an explanation on what is
taken into consideration when calculating the upper and lower confidence
limit of the density estimate? And what do I need to consider when
increasing the number of terms in the model?

Thank you kind researches out there
Gilad

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Model comparison in different habitats
parts:
Hi Gilad, list,

Rather than answer your questions in detail here, can I point you to the sections
of "Introduction to Distance Sampling" where these are discussed.

Some analysis guidelines are given in section 2.5, and model selection (including
selecting adjustment terms) is discussed in section 3.4, 4.6 and 5.6, with
examples given in chapter 8. Confidence limit calculation is covered in section
3.6.1; Distance uses the method of formulae 3.73, 3.74 and 3.75. The options in
Distance for selecting adjustment terms are covered in the online manual -- press
F1 when you have the Model Definition | Detection Function page in front of you.

If you don't have that book and don't want to order it, then an electronic copy of
the old edition (Distance Sampling, 1993) is available free on the internet at
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distancebook/

If this doesn't answer your questions, please get back to me.

- Len
